jobs.title: Environmental Coordinator
jobs.description:
Are you looking to make your mark and grow your career with a company on the rise? We'd love to have you on our team!

Equinox Gold is a growth-focused gold producer headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia, operating a diversified portfolio of high-quality, long-life mines across the Canada, United States, Mexico and Nicaragua. Guided by our core values of integrity, excellence, accountability, and teamwork, we foster a safe, inclusive, and rewarding workplace where a talented, experienced team works together to deliver reliable operations, responsible mining, and long-term value to its shareholders and host communities.

Get in at the ground floor with our South Railroad Project — a construction-ready, open-pit heap leach project located on the world-class Carlin Trend in Nevada, one of the most prolific gold-producing regions on the planet. The project is backed by a completed feasibility study outlining an average of 130,000 ounces of gold per year over the first five years and an initial 10-year mine life. Join us at this pivotal stage and help bring Nevada's next gold mine to life.

Position Summary

As Equinox Gold continues to grow, we are seeking an Environmental Coordinator to join our team. In this role, you will work under the supervision of the Environmental Manager or Environmental Superintendent to support environmental compliance and permitting activities. Responsibilities include assisting with compliance with all mine permits, seeking and maintaining permits for current and future operations, coordinating and managing the work of environmental consultants, and engaging with government agencies as needed.

You will also provide compliance training and field support, including conducting and coordinating environmental sampling, participating in inspections with operations, and communicating regulatory and operating permit requirements. This role will help maintain existing permits and support the permitting process for future mine expansions.

Key Responsibilities

Acquire site specific knowledge of applicable environmental regulations.
Assist in regulatory reporting and compliance activities (air, water, land, wildlife, and waste).
Coordinate environmental sampling, testing, analysis working with staff and/or consultants.
Assist in obtaining and maintaining required and appropriate certifications (e.g. EPA Method 9, DOT HAZMAT, CN Code, ISO 14001, and other necessary programs).
Assist in supporting monitoring and mitigation plans through Agency requirements including but not limited to requirements from BLM, USFWS, SHPO, USACE, NDOW, NDEP, and others.
Maintain environmental records.
Assist in investigating and reporting environmental incidents and assist with mitigation plans.
Assist with Cyanide Code certification and ISO 14001.
Perform safety and environmental audits.
On call rotations.
Assist in permitting minor major federal actions BLM (DNAs, EAs, SEISs), USFWS, USACE, EPA or other as needed.
Assist in permitting minor major state actions with NDEP and Bureaus, NDWR, or other as needed.

Required Experience & Skills

Minimum of 1 year of experience in environmental work, preferably in a coordinator or similar role.
Minimum of 1 year of experience in the mining industry or a related industry.
Experience with environmental permitting, compliance, and regulatory requirements preferred.
Minimum of 3 years of experience with EMS, Datamine Discover 3D, ArcGIS, or other GIS software.
Strong computer skills, including intermediate proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite.
Attention to detail.
Strong critical, strategic, and logical thinking skills.
Effective communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively with operations, consultants, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders.
Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and perform field work, including walking long distances over uneven terrain, climbing stairs, and working in extreme hot and cold temperatures.
Must be authorized to work in the United States for any employer.
Must possess a valid driver's license

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Compliance, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Management or related fields.

At Equinox Gold, our commitment to teamwork means building a workforce that is as diverse as the communities in which we operate. We are committed to an accessible and inclusive recruitment process and welcome applications from all qualified candidates.

jobs.title: District Environmental Manager (Environmental Planning Manager)
jobs.description:
THE POSITION

Make your mark by leading environmental efforts that keep major projects moving forward! The District Environmental Manager position with the Department of Transportation allows you to review plans, guide policies, and support safe construction practices. You will help ensure that environmental commitments are met and that projects stay in line with state and federal requirements. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys both leadership and hands-on problem solving.

DESCRIPTION OF WORK

This role oversees the review of transportation plans and related environmental requirements to ensure full compliance with laws and policies. It supports the development and evaluation of environmental programs and commitments across the District. As a District Environmental Manager, you will perform the following duties:

Environmental Review: Coordinate environmental analyses and guide preparation of required reports
Permit Management: Support waterway permitting activities and ensure permit requirements are met
Program Compliance: Assist with monitoring and improving district programs related to Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System and Strategic Environmental Management Program
Policy Development: Help shape district policies for stormwater control measure design and maintenance
Mitigation Oversight: Manage district commitments involving environmental mitigation and related inspections

Interested in learning more? Additional details regarding this position can be found in the position description .

Work Schedule and Additional Information:

Full-time employment
Work hours are 7:00 AM to 3:00 PM, Monday - Friday, with a 30-minute lunch.
Telework: You may have the opportunity to work from home (telework) part-time. In order to telework, you must have a securely configured high-speed internet connection and work from an approved location inside Pennsylvania. If you are unable to telework, you will have the option to report to the headquarters office in Dunmore. The ability to telework is subject to change at any time. Additional details may be provided during the interview.
Salary:In some cases, the starting salary may be non-negotiable.
You will receive further communication regarding this position via email. Check your email, including spam/junk folders, for these notices.

QUALIFICATIONS

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE, TRAINING & ELIGIBILITY

Minimum Experience and Training Requirements:

Seven years of professional planning experience in local, regional, or state planning including two years in a supervisory capacity; or
Two years of experience as an Environmental Planning Supervisor (Commonwealth job title or equivalent Federal Government job title, as determined by the Office of Administration); or
A Master's degree in planning or one of the environmental sciences and five years of professional planning experience, including two years in a supervisory capacity; or
Any equivalent combination of experience and training.

Other Requirements:

This particular position also requires possession of an active non-commercial Pennsylvania Class C Driver’s License or equivalent.
You must meet the PA residency requirement . For more information on ways to meet PA residency requirements, follow the link and click on Residency Guidelines.
You must be able to perform essential job functions.

jobs.description:
Client: Global Biotech / Pharma

Title: Environmental Health & Safety Project Manager

Location: On site in West Greenwich, RI

Duration: 1 year contract + extensions

You will bring a strong construction safety background and the ability to support project teams through

field engagement, technical guidance, and collaboration with site and corporate safety resources.

Advanced expertise is required in several of the following disciplines:

Construction safety management
Subcontractor and trade-partner safety
Cranes, rigging, and critical lifts
Excavation, trenching, and underground utilities
Job hazard analysis and safety culture development

Duties/Accountabilities include:

Program Management

Support the construction safety program and serve as the on-site safety resource for project

teams and trade partners.

Develop project safety plans covering site logistics, emergency response, permits, and high-risk

work controls.

Ensure compliance with OSHA, applicable regulations, owner standards, and contractual safety

requirements.

Implement field inspections and audits to verify controls before and during construction

activities.

Report safety performance, corrective actions, leading indicators, and emerging risks to project

leadership.

Support other EHS department safety programs and projects as needed.

Client Support

Partner with owners, project managers, superintendents, and subcontractors to deliver safe

construction operations.

Integrate safety into pre-task planning, coordination meetings, toolbox talks, and field routines.
Use safety metrics, audit findings, and field observations to drive site action plans and

improvement.

Lead job and activity hazard analyses; verify controls, permits, and competent-person coverage.
Review scope, schedule, design, and logistics changes for safety impacts before work proceeds.
Assess high-risk work, including falls, struck-by hazards, confined spaces, electrical work,

excavation, and lifting.

Verify safe-work procedures for high-risk activities through inspections and corrective-action

follow-through.

Investigate incidents and near misses; implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence.

Preferred Qualifications

Strong understanding of commercial and industrial construction operations, including multi-

employer work sites.

Ability to partner with and effectively influence staff and management
Knowledge of OSHA construction standards and applicable federal, state, and local construction

safety regulations.

Demonstrated knowledge of construction safety principles, risk-control methods, regulatory

requirements, and practical field application.

Strong communication, presentation, program-development, and construction project-

management skills.

Proficient in Microsoft Office and other computer software systems

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Fauna
jobs.description:
Description

We are seeking a Software Development Engineer to develop cutting-edge machine learning algorithms for robots that operate in human environments and build infrastructure to support our research and development efforts. In this role, you will focus on creating and optimizing intelligent motor control strategies to enable robots to perform complex tasks. Your contributions will advance robotics by enabling fluid, reliable, and safe interactions between robots and their environments. We anticipate that candidates for this role will have experience applying machine learning or AI techniques to control systems, robotics, or related areas in addition to experience with robotic deployments.

Key job responsibilities

Develop techniques and infrastructure that enable deployment of robotic systems on real robots.
Collaborate with multi-disciplinary teams to integrate perception, mapping, navigation, motor control, and human interaction systems with robotic hardware, ensuring alignment with real-world constraints.
Use simulation and real-world testing to refine and validate robot systems.
Stay updated on advancements in robotics, AI, and control systems to apply cutting-edge techniques to robotic system challenges.

About The Team

Fauna Robotics, an Amazon company, is building capable, safe, and genuinely delightful robots for everyday life. Our goal is simple: make robots people actually want to live and interact with in everyday human spaces.

We believe that future won’t arrive until building for robotics becomes far more accessible. Today, too much effort is spent reinventing the fundamentals. We’re changing that by developing tightly integrated hardware and software systems that make it faster, safer, and more intuitive to create real-world robotic products.

Our work spans the full stack: mechanical design, control systems, dynamic modeling, and intelligent software. The focus is not just functionality, but experience. We’re building robots that feel responsive, expressive, and genuinely useful.

At Fauna, you’ll work at the frontier of this space, helping define how robots move, manipulate, and interact with people in natural environments. It’s an opportunity to solve hard problems across hardware and software with a team focused on making robotics accessible and joyful to build.

If you care about making robotics real for everyone and building systems that are as delightful as they are capable, we’re interested in hearing from you.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
Experience programming with at least one software programming language
Prior work experience with robotics (using ROS/ROS2 or otherwise) and/or a deep understanding of robotic subsystems such as computer vision, signal processing, or motor control.
Experience with physics-based simulation tools.
Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, C++.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Computational Neuroscience, or a related field – additional industry experience preferred.
Experience with reinforcement learning, imitation learning, or other AI techniques applied to robotic motor control.
Familiarity with hardware constraints and actuator dynamics for robotic platforms.

new_jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Fauna
new_jobs.description:
Description

We are seeking a Software Development Engineer to develop cutting-edge machine learning algorithms for robots that operate in human environments and build infrastructure to support our research and development efforts. In this role, you will focus on creating and optimizing intelligent motor control strategies to enable robots to perform complex tasks. Your contributions will advance robotics by enabling fluid, reliable, and safe interactions between robots and their environments. We anticipate that candidates for this role will have experience applying machine learning or AI techniques to control systems, robotics, or related areas in addition to experience with robotic deployments.

Key job responsibilities

Develop techniques and infrastructure that enable deployment of robotic systems on real robots.
Collaborate with multi-disciplinary teams to integrate perception, mapping, navigation, motor control, and human interaction systems with robotic hardware, ensuring alignment with real-world constraints.
Use simulation and real-world testing to refine and validate robot systems.
Stay updated on advancements in robotics, AI, and control systems to apply cutting-edge techniques to robotic system challenges.

About The Team

Fauna Robotics, an Amazon company, is building capable, safe, and genuinely delightful robots for everyday life. Our goal is simple: make robots people actually want to live and interact with in everyday human spaces.

We believe that future won’t arrive until building for robotics becomes far more accessible. Today, too much effort is spent reinventing the fundamentals. We’re changing that by developing tightly integrated hardware and software systems that make it faster, safer, and more intuitive to create real-world robotic products.

Our work spans the full stack: mechanical design, control systems, dynamic modeling, and intelligent software. The focus is not just functionality, but experience. We’re building robots that feel responsive, expressive, and genuinely useful.

At Fauna, you’ll work at the frontier of this space, helping define how robots move, manipulate, and interact with people in natural environments. It’s an opportunity to solve hard problems across hardware and software with a team focused on making robotics accessible and joyful to build.

If you care about making robotics real for everyone and building systems that are as delightful as they are capable, we’re interested in hearing from you.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
Experience programming with at least one software programming language
Prior work experience with robotics (using ROS/ROS2 or otherwise) and/or a deep understanding of robotic subsystems such as computer vision, signal processing, or motor control.
Experience with physics-based simulation tools.
Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, C++.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Computational Neuroscience, or a related field – additional industry experience preferred.
Experience with reinforcement learning, imitation learning, or other AI techniques applied to robotic motor control.
Familiarity with hardware constraints and actuator dynamics for robotic platforms.

new_jobs.title: District Environmental Manager (Civil Engineer Manager (Transportation))
new_jobs.description:
THE POSITION

Step into a role that shapes the future of transportation! The District Environmental Manager with the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation helps guide projects that protect communities and natural resources. This position offers a chance to lead important environmental reviews that keep road and bridge work on track. It is an exciting opportunity for someone who enjoys bringing engineering and environmental goals together.

DESCRIPTION OF WORK

This position oversees technical reviews and environmental planning for transportation projects across the district. The work supports responsible project development and helps maintain compliance with important environmental rules. As a District Environmental Manager, you will perform the following duties:

Environmental Reviews: Conduct detailed reviews of reports, plans, and analyses to ensure compliance with environmental laws and guidelines
Technical Guidance: Recommend solutions to engineering issues discovered in design plans and project proposals
Permit Coordination: Work with agencies to secure needed waterway and earth disturbance permits for construction and maintenance activities
Program Oversight: Support district compliance programs related to Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System and Strategic Environmental Management Program through monitoring, training, and policy development
Mitigation Management: Manage and review environmental mitigation commitments, including inspections and coordination with consultants

Work Schedule and Additional Information:

Full-time employment
Work hours are 7:00 AM to 3:00 PM, Monday - Friday, with a 30-minute lunch.
Telework: You may have the opportunity to work from home (telework) part-time. In order to telework, you must have a securely configured high-speed internet connection and work from an approved location inside Pennsylvania. If you are unable to telework, you will have the option to report to the headquarters office in Dunmore. The ability to telework is subject to change at any time. Additional details may be provided during the interview.
Salary:In some cases, the starting salary may be non-negotiable.
You will receive further communication regarding this position via email. Check your email, including spam/junk folders, for these notices.

QUALIFICATIONS

Four years of professional civil engineering experience which includes three years in the appropriate speciality and one year of experience in directing the work of civil engineers.

Special Requirement:

This position requires possession of a valid driver’s license.

You must be able to perform essential job functions.

Information to support your eligibility for the position must be provided on the application (i.e., relevant, detailed experience/education).

Your application must be submitted by the posting closing date . Late applications and other required materials will not be accepted.
